reasons: The candidate multiplies the result by the constant 100, which is not in the Datadog source. The converter must not add numeric constants, so the values would be wrong by a factor of 100.

The Datadog query filters on $host (prefix host, default *), which should become a matcher such as host_name=~"$host". The candidate drops it, so it selects a different set of series. The dataset observes no host label for redis.db.keys, so the label name needs checking before a matcher can be emitted.

redis.db.keys is a per-database gauge in {key}. Summing across db gives the total key count, which matches the Datadog sum over redis.keys, so the quantity itself is plausibly the same. Using a gauge without rate() is correct.
The $key variable (prefix key) is not referenced by the query, so omitting it is correct. The $scope variable has no prefix and default *, so dropping it is also correct.
